fields.Name: constant-contact
fields.Description: Constant Contact V3 REST API (email marketing + contacts/lists/tags/segments/custom-fields/campaigns/reporting). OAuth2 Authorization Code, ROTATING refresh tokens. Cursor pagination via _links.next.href. 10,000 req/day + 4 req/sec rate limit.

OAuthEndpoints.note: OpenAPI securityDefinitions declares two OAuth2 schemes sharing the same authorizationUrl/tokenUrl: oauth2_access_code (flow=accessCode -- the connector's flow) and oauth2_implicit (flow=implicit, browser-only, not used server-side). Every in-scope (non-partner) operation requires one of these two schemes with one of the 5 listed scopes. The `offline_access` scope is NOT enumerated in the OpenAPI securityDefinitions.scopes list but IS documented in the OAuth2 Server Flow guide as required to receive a refresh_token at all -- request it explicitly at authorization time even though the machine spec omits it. A separate `ctctPartnerAuthorizer` + `api_key` (header x-api-key) scheme exists but is used ONLY by the 13 Technology-Partner operations (out of scope, see OutOfScopeObjectFamilies).

Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: POST https://authz.constantcontact.com/oauth2/default/v1/token?refresh_token={refresh_token}&grant_type=refresh_token (Basic-auth header base64(client_id:client_secret)) mints a new access_token. Verbatim from the vendor's OAuth2 Server Flow guide: 'The response will contain a new access_token and refresh_token' (code comment on the vendor's own PHP refreshToken() example, echoed in the JSON response-field description: 'refresh_token -- The response body returns a new refresh_token value'). This is a ROTATING, single-use refresh token: the OLD refresh_token is invalidated the moment a new one is issued, so the connector MUST overwrite its persisted refresh_token with the value from EVERY token-exchange response (both the initial authorization-code exchange AND every subsequent refresh), or the next refresh attempt will be rejected. Access tokens expire 1440 minutes (86,400 seconds) after issuance (401 on an expired token).

RateLimitPolicy.note: Verbatim from the vendor's Rate Limits guide: 'You can use your API key to send up to 10,000 requests per day and 4 requests per second. The request limit resets each day at UTC 00:00:00... If you exceed the 10,000 request per day quota the response body is: {"error_key":"quota_exceeded"...} If you exceed the rate of 4 requests per second the response body is: {"error_key":"throttled"...}'. Root Integration.BatchMaxRequestCount=4 / BatchRequestWaitTime=1(sec) mirror the immediate per-second throttle window (the vendor-stated primary window governing request pacing); the coarser 10,000/day cumulative cap is recorded here for the connector's daily-budget accounting since the root fields model only a single count/window pair. No Retry-After header or other rate-limit-signaling response header is documented in this guide -- recorded honestly as retryAfterHeaderDocumented=false rather than assumed. Certain endpoints additionally carry their own tighter per-endpoint limits per the same guide (not itemized here; the connector should treat 4 req/sec as the safe vendor-wide ceiling).

PaginationDefaults.note: Confirmed vendor-wide across every list (GET collection) operation in the OpenAPI spec: the response includes _links.next.href carrying an opaque base64-encoded `cursor` query parameter (example from the V3 Technical Overview guide: `"_links":{"next":{"href":"/v3/contacts?cursor=bGltaXQ9NSZuZXh0PTImc3RhdHVzJTVCJTVEPWFsbA=="}}`). No offset/page-number pagination variant exists anywhere in the spec. `limit` default/max vary per object (default is 50 for most; see maxPageSizeExamples for the observed range 5-1000) -- always read the per-operation `limit` parameter bounds rather than assuming a single vendor-wide max.

Configuration.APIVersioningNote: Version is embedded in the basePath segment: host=api.cc.email, basePath=/v3 (OpenAPI spec info.version=3.0.161 as of capture -- that is the SPEC's own document version, not a URL-visible API version; the URL-visible version is fixed at 'v3').

IncrementalSyncCapability.scope: narrow -- confirmed by a full scan of every GET-collection operation's query parameters in the OpenAPI spec: only 2 of the 67 in-scope objects document an incremental-filter query parameter. Every other list endpoint (contact_lists, contact_tags, contact_custom_fields, segments, activities, events, social_*, all *_reports/*_reporting endpoints) has NO date/updated/since-style filter parameter and must be re-fetched in full each sync (or via content-hash/keyset strategies at the connector level).

contacts.note: GET /contacts query parameters (confirmed directly in the OpenAPI spec operation parameters). The V3 Technical Overview guide's own worked example uses updated_after: '.../v3/contacts?status=unsubscribed&updated_after=2018-3-31&...'.

emails.note: GET /emails query parameters -- a narrower, differently-named pair (after_date/before_date, not updated_after/updated_before) confirmed directly in the OpenAPI spec operation parameters; do not assume the contacts param names apply here.

IncrementalSyncCapability.defaultStrategyForAllOtherObjects: full-refresh (re-fetch and content-hash/dedupe) -- no incremental query parameter is documented for any of the other 65 in-scope objects.

Configuration.WebhooksNote: The only webhook-management endpoints in the OpenAPI spec (/partner/webhooks/subscriptions, /partner/webhooks/subscriptions/{topic_id}, .../tests) live under the 'Technology Partners Webhooks' tag, gated behind the ctctPartnerAuthorizer+api_key security scheme and the Technology Partner Program (see OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.partner_webhooks). No general-purpose (non-partner) webhook surface exists in this spec for the core V3 sync scope.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: The 'Bulk Activities' tag (12 leaf endpoints) implements an async job state machine: POST /activities/* (contact_delete, contacts_file_import, contacts_json_import, contact_exports, list_delete, add/remove_list_memberships, contacts_taggings_add/remove, contacts_tags_delete, custom_fields_delete) each returns an Activity job resource polled via GET /activities/{activity_id}, with states processing/completed/cancelled/failed/time_out/unknown (ActivityStatus/ActivityGenericStatus definitions). This is a genuine vendor-wide bulk-operation surface distinct from single-record CRUD, confirmed directly in the OpenAPI spec (Bulk Activities tag).

ErrorResponseShape.note: Confirmed via the Rate Limits guide's two worked 429 response bodies (quota_exceeded / throttled) and the per-operation response-code descriptions repeated across the OpenAPI spec (400 malformed/validation, 401 invalid access token, 403 forbidden/insufficient scope/deactivated app, 404 not found, 415 unsupported media type, 429 rate limit, 500/503 internal/service error). No structured error-body schema beyond error_key/error_message is documented for non-429 codes in the sources examined; other 4xx/5xx bodies were not independently confirmed to share this exact shape (only the 429 case has a vendor-published example body) -- treat as a partial gap for the non-429 error-body shape. [Amended by MetadataWriter bijection audit: a full programmatic scan of every operations responses object across all 98 paths in sources/openapi.json (extract-remaining-config-facts.mjs) found 3 additional >=400 codes not previously listed here -- 405 (Method Not Allowed, 2 operations), 406 (Not Acceptable, 2 operations), 409 (Conflict, 22 operations) -- now included for completeness. The 429 body-shape evidence remains the only status code with a fully-documented error body; the others are confirmed present as response keys but their body schema was not independently verified beyond error_key/error_message.]

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: A full-text scan of the saved OpenAPI spec for ETag / If-Match / If-Unmodified-Since found zero matches. No optimistic-concurrency mechanism (header or body version field) is documented anywhere in the V3 spec. Conflict resolution must use snapshot-3-way only if bidirectional sync is ever enabled.

DeleteSemanticsDetail.contacts: soft -- DELETE /contacts/{contact_id} description states deleted contacts 'won't receive email... but... can be revived, or added back to an account' (tombstone/archive-with-revive pattern, no dedicated IsDeleted field name documented -- the connector must treat a successful 204 DELETE as a state transition, not a row removal, and expect the contact_id to remain resolvable via the revive path)
DeleteSemanticsDetail.email_campaigns: soft -- DELETE /emails/{campaign_id} description states 'Constant Contact users can restore deleted email campaigns using the UI' (confirmed by a script-driven keyword scan over every DELETE operation description, see CODE_EVIDENCE extract-integration-config-facts.mjs deleteOps)
DeleteSemanticsDetail.contact_lists: hard -- 'Deletes the specified contact list and its membership' (async job), no revive/restore language found by the deleteOps keyword scan
DeleteSemanticsDetail.contact_tags: hard -- un-assigns from all contacts then deletes the tag, no revive/restore language found by the scan
DeleteSemanticsDetail.contact_custom_fields: hard -- 'Delete a custom field from the user's account', no revive/restore language found by the scan
DeleteSemanticsDetail.segments: hard -- 'Deleted segments do not display in the results', no revive/restore language found by the scan

Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: Confirmed via a script-driven keyword scan (reviv|restore|undelete) over every DELETE operation's OpenAPI description (extract-integration-config-facts.mjs deleteOps, 10 DELETE operations scanned) -- 2 of 10 (contacts, email_campaigns) document user-facing restore/revive capability (soft-delete/tombstone semantics); the remaining 8 (contact_lists, contact_tags, contact_custom_fields, segments, email schedules/non_opener_resends/abtest, partner webhook subscription) have no such language (hard delete). DeleteSemantics is 'mixed' at the vendor level -- per-IO DeleteBehavior should follow this per-object detail, not a single blanket value.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Every object defaults to Pull (read-only) regardless of documented write capability, per the read-first bidirectional-is-opt-in discipline. Bidirectional write-back requires a sandbox-validated opt-in (allowWrite) even for the write-capable families listed in WriteCapability.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReason: ConcurrencyControl=none (no ETag/If-Match/version field documented anywhere in the V3 spec) rules out a reliable MostRecent resolution. DestWins is the safe default if/when bidirectional sync is later enabled for a write-capable family -- it overwrites the MJ destination with Constant Contact's source-of-truth on pull rather than attempting an unverifiable timestamp-based merge.
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNote: Not applicable -- Constant Contact does not expose a customer-defined custom-OBJECT capability anywhere in the V3 spec (no equivalent of HubSpot custom objects / Salesforce custom objects). The only customer-extensible surface is custom FIELDS on the Contact entity (see CustomFieldMarkerPattern).
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: Not applicable in the 'marker distinguishing custom-vs-system fields within one collection' sense -- the entire /contact_custom_fields collection (Contacts Custom Fields tag) IS the tenant's custom-field surface by construction; there is no commingled system/custom flag to filter on (confirmed: the CustomField definition has no IsSystem/IsBuiltIn-style property). Per-tenant custom field NAMES/labels are runtime-discovery-only (per connector conventions) -- the CRUD shape is Declared, the actual field catalog is not.

PKNamingObservation.note: A script-verified check across every GET-by-id path in the spec (extract-integration-config-facts.mjs) found the path-parameter name (e.g. contact_id, list_id, tag_id, custom_field_id, campaign_id, event_id, segment_id) present as a same-named property on the corresponding response-body definition in 11 of 15 cases (73.3%). This does NOT clear the >=95% statistical-significance bar required to emit a vendor-wide `universalPK` hint for runtime D4 -- the 4 mismatches are reporting/stats/export query endpoints (ActivityGetExport, SmsEngagementHistory, CampaignStatsQueryResultEmail, CampaignActivityStatsQueryResultEmail) that are not primary syncable resources with a stable single-field PK. Recorded here as an informational observation only; universalPK is deliberately left UNSET so PK determination falls to per-IOF path-parameter alignment (which IS reliable per-resource, see the individual IOF IsPrimaryKey emissions) and runtime D4, not a blanket vendor-wide hint.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.detail: Technology Partners Webhooks tag (5 endpoints -> 2 leaves: partner_webhook_subscriptions, partner_webhook_subscription_tests). Requires Technology Partner Program approval (partner-request signup form + Partner Management Team review, 'may take several weeks') and uses a separate security scheme (ctctPartnerAuthorizer + api_key/x-api-key) distinct from the core oauth2_access_code scheme every in-scope operation uses.

Technology Partners tag (8 endpoints -> 6 leaves: partner_accounts, partner_accounts_plan, partner_accounts_status_cancel, partner_accounts_operations_sync, partner_accounts_users_sso, partner_accounts_contacts_unsubscribe). Same gated program + security scheme as partner_webhooks -- a partner account-provisioning API, not a general customer-data sync surface.

SMS Reporting tag (1 endpoint -> 1 leaf: sms_campaign_summaries, path /reports/summary_reports/sms_campaign_summaries). SMS is a distinct, plan/product-gated marketing channel (SMS campaign sending + its summary reporting) not part of the core email/contacts sync surface. Note: contacts_sms_engagement_history (a Contacts-tag sub-resource) IS in scope -- only the SMS-campaign-specific reporting leaf is excluded.

A wholly separate, older API version hosted at v2.developer.constantcontact.com -- confirmed absent from this V3 spec entirely (no v2 host/paths appear anywhere in openapi.json). Not to be confused with the V3-native 'Events' tag (event management), which IS in scope and lives on the same api.cc.email/v3 host/OAuth scheme as everything else.

Third-party no-code automation platform. Constant Contact does not host a Zapier-specific API surface of its own -- Zapier consumes the same V3 API plus its own trigger/action wrapper hosted on Zapier's platform. Nothing in openapi.json references Zapier; there is no credential-free Constant-Contact-hosted endpoint to enumerate.
Same rationale as zapier -- Integromat/Make's own platform, not a Constant-Contact-hosted surface.

Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeReason: Constant Contact's V3 API has no single complete 'describe all objects/fields' endpoint analogous to a schema-introspection call -- the OpenAPI spec is the only complete-schema source and it is fetched (as static Declared metadata) at BUILD time, not by the connector's own runtime DiscoverObjects/DiscoverFields methods. The connector's runtime discovery (when implemented) can at best enumerate a SCOPED subset per tenant (e.g. a tenant's actual custom-field catalog via GET /contact_custom_fields, which is real per-tenant data, not a schema description of the vendor's full object universe). Per the authoritative-discovery rule, absence of an object/field in a live discovery pass therefore proves NOTHING about whether the vendor still exposes it -- it could simply mean that tenant hasn't used that feature. DiscoveryIsAuthoritative is hard-coded false so a comprehensive-refresh NEVER deactivates a Declared IO/IOF based on runtime discovery absence for this connector.

fields.Name: account_physical_address
fields.Description: GET the Physical Address for the Account Singleton with no addressable identity: the account is implied by the access token, so /account/summary/physical_address has no path variable to key on, and the AccountPhysicalAddress schema declares no identifier (address_line1..country_code only). CC documents it as an account-level component also readable via /account/summary?extra_fields=physical_address. Declaring encoded_account_id here would put the key on a field the endpoint never returns — a null primary key, which is the same silent failure in a different disguise. The writable account-level object is account_summary (keyed on encoded_account_id).

Configuration.trackIdNote: Constant Contact event tracks are not an enumerable list resource in the V3 catalog: {track_id} has no parent IntegrationObject to iterate over, so this nested object is structurally non-list-syncable (only event_id resolves; track_id is PARENT_UNRESOLVED). Keyless (no PK) and write-only (PUT payment_status).
